content.text: I'll help you create an open-top box with the specified dimensions. Let me first calculate the inner dimensions and then create the box using blocks.

input.PythonCode:
# Given dimensions
outer_length = 220  # mm (x-direction)
outer_width = 300   # mm (y-direction)
outer_height = 160  # mm (z-direction)
wall_thickness = 8  # mm
bottom_thickness = 12  # mm

# Calculate inner dimensions
inner_length = outer_length - 2 * wall_thickness
inner_width = outer_width - 2 * wall_thickness
inner_height = outer_height - bottom_thickness

print(f"Outer dimensions: {outer_length} x {outer_width} x {outer_height} mm")
print(f"Wall thickness: {wall_thickness} mm")
print(f"Bottom thickness: {bottom_thickness} mm")
print(f"\nInner cavity dimensions:")
print(f"Inner length (x): {inner_length} mm")
print(f"Inner width (y): {inner_width} mm")
print(f"Inner height (z): {inner_height} mm")
print(f"\nInner cavity position (from origin):")
print(f"x: {wall_thickness} mm")
print(f"y: {wall_thickness} mm")
print(f"z: {bottom_thickness} mm")

The open-top box has been created successfully! The box has:
- Outer dimensions: 220 x 300 x 160 mm
- Wall thickness: 8 mm on all sides
- Bottom thickness: 12 mm
- Open top (no top wall)

The box was created by:
1. First creating a solid outer block (220 x 300 x 160 mm)
2. Then subtracting an inner cavity (204 x 284 x 148 mm) positioned 8 mm from the sides and 12 mm from the bottom

This results in an open-top box with the specified wall and bottom thicknesses.
